Title: Using Garnet as a Geothermometer
Content: A geothermometer mineral is a mineral with slight differences in composition that can be used to estimate the temperature at which some types of metamorphic rock form. Garnet is a geothermometer mineral because there are several kinds of garnet that contain different amounts of iron and magnesium. The “garnet coefficient” indicates the ratio of iron to magnesium found in the garnet. When the garnet coefficient is high, there is a greater percentage of iron compared to magnesium. The garnet coefficient is an indicator of the temperature at which a metamorphic rock formed.
